title: What the Tuskegee Airman Can Teach Today's Force
gist: An Airman Pulse podcast episode note previews Air Force historian Dr. Daniel Haulman explaining how primary-source records led him to correct enduring myths about the Tuskegee Airmen, and why getting the historical facts right honors their legacy rather than diminishing it.

themes.theme: Correcting the historical record on the Tuskegee Airmen

insights.claim: Dr. Daniel Haulman, a historian with the Air Force Historical Research Agency, says primary-source records led him to correct enduring myths about the Tuskegee Airmen.
insights.speaker: Daniel Haulman and Patrick McSpadden
insights.so_what: No market relevance; a historical-accuracy narrative about a well-known WWII unit, useful only as cultural/organizational-history context.

insights.claim: Haulman's central argument is that getting the historical facts right about the Tuskegee Airmen 'honors their legacy rather than diminishes it,' framing rigorous correction of popular myths as a form of respect rather than debunking.
insights.speaker: Daniel Haulman and Patrick McSpadden
